action: Rakuten Securities, as reported by SBbit, recommends setting up passkey authentication and says it will not put URLs in emails about this incident or phone to ask for personal or login information.
date_note: Date the company says it learned a third party may have accessed its systems; Security NEXT published on 2026-11-18.
exec: Rakuten Securities says its second report found names, birth dates, addresses and phone numbers among the leaked customer data.
plain: Rakuten Securities' second report says about 4.41 million records include names, birth dates, addresses and phone numbers. The company says it has not confirmed a leak of passwords or PINs.
summary: Rakuten Securities said on 17 November that a third party may have accessed its systems. Its second report of 24 November, relayed by Impress Watch, says about 4.41 million records include names and addresses; J-CAST says about 1.19 million belong to people who had not opened an account, and the company told J-CAST it is investigating why. No password or PIN leak was confirmed.
title: Rakuten Securities second report: leaked customer data includes names, addresses and phone numbers

validation.note: Security NEXT and ITmedia NEWS independently report the company's 17 Nov disclosure (detected 16 Nov); Impress Watch relays the 24 Nov second report. The company's own press release PDF could not be read by the reviewer and was removed from sources. Impress Watch says 441万 is a count of records (件) while INTERNET Watch's headline says accounts (口座).

review.note: action advice: channel list not on pages read; now SBbit-reported advice only. Figures, date, status checked against Impress Watch, INTERNET Watch, Security NEXT
